chunks: "It is written on the gate of Paradise: charity is rewarded tenfold, and a loan is rewarded eighteenfold."

key_terms.الصَّدَقَةُ: charity given for the sake of Allah
key_terms.الْقَرْضُ: a loan given to someone in need

ai.seo_question: Why does lending have greater reward than charity in this hadith?
ai.summary: Imam Jaʿfar ibn Muḥammad al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام teaches that both charity and lending are greatly rewarded by Allah, with lending receiving an even greater reward. The hadith highlights the virtue of helping others financially in ways that relieve need and preserve dignity, while pointing to reward in Paradise.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.1697 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said:
"It is written on the gate of Paradise: Charity is rewarded tenfold, and a loan is rewarded eighteenfold."
